Sercotec and Walmart Chile sign agreement to offer sales spaces for entrepreneurs
Sercotec has partnered with Walmart Chile to provide small business owners space at Lider stores for product sales through special fairs. The agreement was announced during Small Business Week as part of efforts to support local entrepreneurship.
A collaboration between Sercotec and Walmart Chile will allow beneficiaries of Ministry of Economy programs to sell their products at Lider stores through specially organized fairs, giving them access to thousands of potential customers. The Ministry of Economy, Development and Tourism, through Sercotec, signed the agreement with Walmart Chile on Oct. 15 as part of an initiative to create new commercial opportunities for entrepreneurs who participate in Sercotec programs.
The partnership will enable micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises to display and sell their products at Lider store locations via dedicated fairs within the stores. This aims to help these businesses reach new audiences and strengthen their market presence.
The announcement took place during a Sercotec entrepreneur fair held at the Lider Santa Amalia branch in La Florida district. Attendees included Daniel Mas, Minister of Economy and Mining; Henry Azurmendi, General Manager of Sercotec; and Daniela Riutort, Corporate Affairs Manager at Walmart Chile.
Daniel Mas said he is proud of all those who have chosen entrepreneurship: “President José Antonio Kast has asked us to put the country back on a growth path, and here we are doing that. We are giving every entrepreneur an opportunity with this agreement so they can sell more, have more working capital, grow further—and why not dream that one day they might export their products? We will continue working so that in Chile entrepreneurial effort is always rewarded by generating more jobs, more competition and greater prosperity.”
Azurmendi said: “The agreement we are celebrating today is the best example of a public-private alliance that drives the development of small- and medium-sized enterprises. With this alliance, micro-entrepreneurs working with Sercotec will connect with large companies by accessing high-traffic commercial spaces in Walmart branches—a great opportunity for visibility and entry into new markets supporting their growth. We value this linkage and invite people to visit entrepreneur fairs set up in different regions because together we advance the development and strengthening of SMEs in our country.”
Riutort said: “At Walmart Chile we believe our commitment to communities goes far beyond our supermarkets. Through initiatives like Hecho en Mi Barrio we seek new commercialization opportunities for local entrepreneurs—accompanying them through different stages as they grow. This agreement with Sercotec allows us to expand that impact during 2027 by facilitating access to sales spaces nationwide. We want more entrepreneurs growing their businesses, generating income, contributing economically because when SMEs grow so do their communities.”
This initiative seeks to create additional channels for promotion and commercialization among small businesses supported by Sercotec by helping them reach wider audiences.
The activity was part of Small Business Week (Semana de la Pyme), which includes over 380 events across the country aimed at strengthening entrepreneurship ecosystems through public-private collaboration.
